name: SWF World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The top belt of the diary's SWF. Jack Bruce holds it when the diary opens, a reign the diary's later posts date from last August, and he keeps it through Brandon James at Awesome Impact and Remo at The World is Watching, where Vengeance's interference ends the second match by disqualification. At Master of Puppets 2008 he beats Vengeance in a Supreme Cell match, and the diary's June posts book him against Eric Eisen for it at Times of Trouble 2008. Bruce beats Eric Eisen at Times of Trouble 2008, keeps the belt against Antonio Marquez and John McClean on Supreme TV in Week 3 of June and against Jay Chord in Week 2 of July, and sees Richard Eisen pick him in the brand split, which ties the title to the Supreme brand even if he loses it. Eisen then announces Supreme Double Jeopardy for The Supreme Challenge 28, in which Bruce must defend the belt twice in one night, first against Vengeance, with Eric Tyler added to that first match by Phil Vibert and the second opponent left for Eisen to choose on the night. Bruce beats Eric Tyler and Vengeance in the first Supreme Double Jeopardy match at The Supreme Challenge 28, then loses the belt to Rich Money in the second after Richard Eisen's indecision lets Money into it, ending a reign the SWF.com review puts at some eleven months. Money refuses to defend the belt anywhere but pay-per-view, makes Bruce and Randy Bumfhole each beat Remo for a shot, swaps the belt for a black one set with diamonds on Supreme TV in Week 4 of July 2008, and, when Bruce and Bumfhole fight to a double disqualification in Week 2 of August, sees Richard Eisen make Welcome to the Jungle 2008 a Threefold Threat among the three. Money keeps the belt at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 in a Threefold Threat against Jack Bruce and Randy Bumfhole, pinning Bruce with Bruce's own New York Minute, and Remo hands him his custom belt. He beats Guide on Supreme TV in Week 3 of August with Bruce watching from the ramp and, on a video from the Las Vegas casino he part owns, turns down Bruce's challenge for Under Control 2008; Pistol Pete Hall, who has asked for a match, is billed against him for the belt on Supreme TV in Week 2 of September.

name: SWF North American Championship
epitaph: The belt Rich Money holds in Big Money Incorporated when the diary opens, defended against Eric Tyler, Randy Bumfhole and Christian Faith before Steve Frehley takes it at The World is Watching and then refuses to defend it on Supreme TV, leaving Richard Eisen to announce its future. Eisen then sets up an eight-man Grand Prix for it, which Marc DuBois wins over Eric Eisen at Master of Puppets 2008, and DuBois defends it into June 2008. He keeps it in a three-way against Runaway Train and Antonio Marquez at Times of Trouble 2008, against Valiant on Supreme TV in Week 4 of June and, when Chris Morrisette wins by disqualification after DuBois hits him with the belt, in Week 1 of July 2008; the card of The Supreme Challenge 28 puts the title in a Threefold Threat against Zimmy Bumfhole and Antonio Marquez. DuBois keeps it at The Supreme Challenge 28 in a Threefold Threat against Zimmy Bumfhole and Antonio Marquez, when Darryl Devine's interference lets him throw the referee in front of Marquez's shooting star press; Welcome to the Jungle 2008 is set as another Threefold Threat, with Devine, who has complained to Richard Eisen, and Marquez, who wins the Supreme TV three-way against Zimmy Bumfhole and Sean Deeley for the place. DuBois keeps it in the Threefold Threat at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 when Darryl Devine taps to the Model Solution sleeper, beats Zimmy Bumfhole on Supreme TV in Week 4 of August and Scout of The New Wave in Week 1 of September, and is billed against Art Reed in Week 2.

name: SWF World Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The pair of belts held by Sexual Aggression, who took them from The Amazing Bumfholes at Nothing to Lose in February 2008 and defend them on Supreme TV, at Awesome Impact and at The World is Watching. They keep them against The Amazing Bumfholes at Master of Puppets 2008, and Valiant & Giedroyc take them from Sexual Aggression on the first SWF Legends in June 2008, after Joe Sexy walks out on Angry Gilmore mid-match. Valiant & Giedroyc keep the belts when Giedroyc's stoppage win ends the four-way at Times of Trouble 2008, then against The Heartbreakers on Supreme TV in Week 1 of July and The Upper Class in Week 2; the card of The Supreme Challenge 28 sets them against The New Wave and Badd Kompany in a Threefold Threat. Valiant & Giedroyc keep the belts at The Supreme Challenge 28 when Valiant pins Joss Thompson in a Threefold Threat against The New Wave and Badd Kompany, and are booked against Sin Inc for Welcome to the Jungle 2008. Valiant & Giedroyc keep the belts at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 against Sin Inc when Giedroyc rolls up John McClean, beat The Upper Class in Week 3 of August and The Heartbreakers in Week 1 of September, and Richard Eisen names The New Wave the next challengers, for Under Control 2008.

name: SWF Shooting Star Championship
epitaph: The lowest-ranked singles belt, which the diary's characters call the least important in the promotion. Marc DuBois holds it through ladder matches against Enygma and Antonio Marquez until Darryl Devine wins it at The World is Watching. Darryl Devine keeps it through the ladder match with Enygma at Master of Puppets 2008 and on SWF Legends in June 2008, when Phil Vibert names it the title of a new Sky Club Division for the high-fliers. Devine keeps it in the three-way ladder match at Times of Trouble 2008 but loses it to Kid Toma on SWF Legends in June 2008, after the Samoan Family's interference; Toma keeps it against Brett Biggz and American Elemental and then against Jacob Jett, and the belt is not on the card of The Supreme Challenge 28. Toma keeps it against Remmy Skye on SWF Legends in Week 4 of July 2008, the night Eric Tyler hands him a redesigned belt, and Bart Biggz earns a shot for Welcome to the Jungle 2008 by beating Akima Brave by disqualification in Week 1 of August. Acid, a masked high-flier new to the SWF, pins Kid Toma in a Threefold Threat with Bart Biggz at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 and takes the belt; he keeps it against El Leon and Mainstream Hernandez on SWF Legends in Week 3 of August, Remmy Skye in Week 4 and John Greed and Mainstream Hernandez in Week 1 of September, while Bart Biggz asks for a singles match.

name: SWF Generations Championship
epitaph: A new belt for Generation Supreme, shown off by Richard Eisen and Jack Bruce on the second Friday show of the diary and won by Ace Newton in a ten-man battle royal at The World is Watching. Robbie Retro takes it from Newton on Supreme TV in June 2008. Retro keeps it against Sean Deeley on Supreme TV in Week 1 of July 2008, while he and Newton each claim to be the face of Generation Supreme and both are left off the card of The Supreme Challenge 28. Retro keeps it against Ash Campbell on Supreme TV in Week 3 of July 2008 but loses it to Ace Newton in a Threefold Threat with Jay Chord a week later, Newton pinning Retro with his feet on the ropes; in Week 1 of August the Four Kings and Playboy Jake Sawyer give Newton a new belt, which Richard Eisen calls the new official Generations Championship. Newton keeps it against Kirk Jameson on Supreme TV in Week 3 of August 2008 and, in the SWF.com recaps of Generation Supreme, against El Leon and Swoop McCarthy, and is billed against Gino Montero for it in Week 2 of September.

name: SWF Legends Championship
epitaph: A belt Phil Vibert, the general manager of SWF Legends, unveils on Supreme TV in May 2008 for the hard-brawling veterans who do not compete for the world title, first shown as a tattered old belt. Chris Caufield wins it in a four-way elimination match over John McClean, Runaway Train and Enforcer Roberts on the first SWF Legends in June 2008, and Vibert then hands him the finished belt. Caufield keeps it against Enygma on SWF Legends in June 2008, against Texas Pete by count-out in Week 4 of June, when the Golden Faction's Rocky Golden berates Pete for failing, and against Enforcer Roberts in Week 2 of July, a match the diary says would have moved Roberts to the Legends brand; Bloodstone of the Golden Faction is booked to challenge him at The Supreme Challenge 28. Caufield loses it at The Supreme Challenge 28 to Bloodstone, whose camel clutch ends the match by referee stoppage while Caufield insists he never submitted; Bloodstone keeps it against Brett Biggz and Pistol Pete Hall, and Robbie Retro says Phil Vibert has put him into the match with Caufield at Welcome to the Jungle 2008. Bloodstone keeps it at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 in a Threefold Threat against Robbie Retro and Chris Caufield, pinning Caufield, and against Robbie Retro on SWF Legends in Week 4 of August, when the referee stops the match in the Bloodstone Mutilation.

name: SWF Supreme Championship
epitaph: A second top championship Phil Vibert announces on SWF Legends in June 2008, after the terms Richard Eisen put into the brand split attach every singles title to one brand and so tie the World Heavyweight Championship to Supreme TV. Vibert unveils the gold-and-platinum belt on SWF Legends in Week 4 of June 2008, calls it the most expensive in professional wrestling history, and sets the first champion to be decided at The Supreme Challenge 28, where the card puts Christian Faith against Brandon James for it. Christian Faith wins it at The Supreme Challenge 28, beating Brandon James with the Test of Faith sleeper, and Phil Vibert takes the belt from the referee to present it. Faith keeps it against Bloodstone and Eric Eisen on SWF Legends in Week 3 of July 2008, Troy Tornado in Week 4 and Texas Pete in Week 1 of August; Vengeance is booked against him for Welcome to the Jungle 2008, and Brandon James and Steve Frehley meet there for a shot at the belt at Under Control 2008. Faith keeps it against Vengeance at Welcome to the Jungle 2008, after which Vengeance puts him through the timekeeper's table, and against Bryan Holmes on SWF Legends in Week 3 of August; in Week 4 he keeps it by disqualification in a Threefold Threat with Steve Frehley and Rocky Golden, and Under Control 2008 is billed as a Threefold Threat for it among Faith, Brandon James and Steve Frehley.

name: SWF Sky Club Tag Team Championship
aka: SWF Sky Club Tag Team Titles
SWF Sky Club Division Tag Team Championships
epitaph: A pair of tag belts Eric Tyler, the new General Manager of SWF Legends, unveils on SWF Legends in July 2008 in his first 'Mr. Tyler Says' segment, so that the Sky Club division's tag teams, tied to the Legends brand, have belts of their own instead of the World Tag Team Championships of the Supreme brand. Tyler sets a four-team tournament with its deciding match at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 among The Upper Class, High Concept, The Tokyo Underground and Pure Energy; High Concept and The Tokyo Underground qualify on SWF Legends in Week 2 of August 2008 by beating The Upper Class and Pure Energy, and High Concept, Elmo Benson and Groucho Bling, beat The Tokyo Underground at Welcome to the Jungle 2008 to become the first champions. They keep the belts against Double Deuce on SWF Legends in Week 4 of August and lose a non-title match to Rocky Golden and Bloodstone in Week 1 of September.
